newsitem.title: MEXICO: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Weekly Mexican export, import feeder summary - USDA.

text.p: USDA said Friday that steer calves exported to the United States from Mexico sold steady this week compared to last week.
Exports for the week were estimated at 4,500 head into Texas and New Mexico states, against 2,180 head in the same week in 1996.
"Trade moderate, demand good. Bulk of supply consisted of medium and large steers weighing 300-600 lb. Around 30 percent of cattle crossed were previously contracted or sold on video," USDA said.
Prices for feeder steers weighing 300-400 lb were 94-104 cents/lb, for 400-500 lb they were 84-94 cents/lb.
Imports into Mexico of slaughter cattle were estimated to have totaled 2,500 head for the week, it added.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
